tour.title: Start here: the repository and the three shelves
tour.description: Read the repository README to see what lives where, then the site index that splits the documentation into plattform, produkt and betrieb. Note that everything under site/content/docs is generated by the sync script from the source folders, so this is where you read but not where you edit.

tour.title: What the product actually is
tour.description: The product overview and summary describe online counselling as ORISO delivers it: help-seekers, counsellors, Beratungsstellen and Traeger. The roles and permissions page is the one to keep open while reading everything else, because almost every later decision is about who may see what.

tour.title: The platform overview and the repository map
tour.description: The architecture hub gives the system-level picture and the repository map names every ORISO repository and what it owns. Pair it with the backend-services and database pages to know which service holds which data before you read any decision about that data.

tour.title: The ADR set and how to read it
tour.description: The decisions README indexes all twenty-three platform ADRs and records their status. Read it before any individual ADR: several records are partially superseded or extended by later ones, and one number was reassigned after a collision.

tour.title: Modalities: the axis everything else hangs on
tour.description: ADR-001 untangles consulting_type into modality, topic and agency; ADR-006 turns the modality into a persisted conversation_type enum with four values. Read these first among the ADRs, because live chat, group chat and the settings cascade all key off this axis.

tour.title: Departments: agency times topic
tour.description: ADR-003 defines a Fachbereich as the unique pairing of an agency and a topic that carries its own imprint and DPP; ADR-014 reverses its single-select topic picker, makes legal texts shareable objects and fixes topic-before-consent. ADR-009 completes the picture by making topics global platform objects rather than tenant-owned data.

tour.title: Legal texts, consent gates and Traeger governance
tour.description: ADR-021 names the four levels of legal text and adds generic versioning; ADR-022 fixes exactly two consent gates and stores consent as a session pointer so a new version re-prompts; ADR-023 renames the platform-to-Traeger relationship and makes the AVV an annex. This block only makes sense after the department block above.

tour.title: Messaging on Matrix
tour.description: ADR-005 comes before ADR-004 in dependency order: a real DNS server_name with federation off is the prerequisite for binding device keys to stable MXIDs. Then ADR-004 keeps the custom chat UI over matrix-js-sdk Megolm, and ADR-017 replaces the home-grown thread prefix with native m.thread relations.

tour.title: Confidentiality inside and around a room
tour.description: ADR-002 makes every department counsellor a real member from room creation and puts the confidentiality boundary in access control rather than crypto; ADR-008 moves supervision side-channels out of the help-seeker's room; ADR-016 generalises the side room to the pre-acceptance Team-Besprechung and hard-closes it on acceptance.

tour.title: Features that sit on top: live chat, groups, media, calls, Erstantwort
tour.description: ADR-007 makes liveness read the authoritative availability model; ADR-012 extends the group chat for self-help groups with a future timeline; ADR-015 and ADR-019 govern media flags and fail-closed scanning; ADR-020 separates appointment, call session and invitation; ADR-018 rebuilds the first response. Read these once the axes and the room model are clear.

tour.title: Deployment: Helm, one domain, one certificate
tour.description: ADR-011 makes ORISO-Helm the canonical deployment definition and replaces per-service subdomains with path-based routing on a single host. Follow it with the kubernetes-deployment page and the betrieb deployment chapter to see the charts applied in order, and ADR-013 for the custom Keycloak image that 2FA depends on.

tour.title: Operating it: local stack, verification, troubleshooting
tour.description: Finish with the operational layer: the local development page and runbook for getting a stack up on your machine, verification testing for proving an environment works, and the troubleshooting and onboarding pages for the failure modes the team keeps hitting.
